name: CamScanner
tagline: Phone camera document scanner that crops, deskews and cleans pages into multi-page PDFs with OCR.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The whole product is a camera, four corner points, a perspective transform, a contrast curve and a PDF writer. Every one of those pieces is a solved, open, well documented problem: OpenCV finds the page quad, a threshold pass makes it look like paper, Tesseract adds a searchable text layer, and jsPDF assembles the file. A local PWA gets you the scan-to-clean-PDF loop in a single sitting, with no watermark, no upload, no ads, no upsell modal on page three. What you will not match in one shot is the auto-capture feel, the tuned enhancement presets, and the cloud folder that syncs to your laptop. Worth noting the phone in your pocket already ships a decent scanner in its notes and files apps, which is the real reason paying for this is a choice, not a necessity.
coreLoopDIY: A local PWA that grabs frames from the phone camera, lets you drag four corners, warps and cleans the page, runs OCR, and exports a multi-page searchable PDF stored on device.
requirements: A phone or laptop with a camera and an HTTPS origin (camera APIs need it, localhost counts)
OpenCV.js and Tesseract.js bundles, both a few MB on first load
Somewhere to serve static files, or just run it locally
whatYouLose: Automatic shutter that fires the instant the page is square and steady, which is most of the perceived quality
Hand-tuned enhancement presets for receipts, whiteboards, ID cards and faint pencil
Cloud sync, shared folders and getting the scan onto your desktop without emailing yourself
OCR that is genuinely good across dozens of languages and handwriting, and fast on a mid-range phone
Extras like e-signature, page reordering across many long documents, and fax or cloud print integrations
moatNotes: The moat is tuning, not technology: hundreds of small decisions about when to auto-capture and how hard to crush the background.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because scanning is a thing people do twice a year in a panic, usually to send a landlord or an accountant something, and in that moment nobody wants to debug their own camera app. CamScanner is installed, it has the presets, and the paid tier mostly buys the removal of watermarks and ads rather than any capability. The honest competitor is not a DIY build, it is the scanner already built into iOS Notes and Google Drive, which is free and good enough for most pages.
notes: Rare case where the DIY version and the free OS feature both beat the subscription on value.
prompt:
Build a local, offline-first document scanner as a PWA. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, nothing leaves the device.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS modules, opencv.js loaded from a local vendored file, tesseract.js for OCR, jspdf for export, idb-keyval for storage. No UI framework, no state library.

Screens:
1. Capture: getUserMedia with facingMode environment, full-bleed video preview, big shutter button, torch toggle if the track supports it, and a file input fallback for desktop.
2. Crop: show the captured still on a canvas with four draggable corner handles. On load, run an OpenCV pass (grayscale, Gaussian blur, Canny, findContours, approxPolyDP) to guess the largest four-sided contour and pre-place the handles there. If nothing is found, default the handles to the image corners.
3. Enhance: apply a getPerspectiveTransform warp to a target aspect based on the quad, then offer four modes: Original, Grayscale, Document (adaptive threshold), and High Contrast (CLAHE plus gamma). Live preview, one tap to switch.
4. Document view: a page list with thumbnails, drag to reorder, delete, and Add page which returns to Capture.
5. Export: build a multi-page PDF with jspdf, one warped page image per page sized to fit A4. Optional checkbox Searchable text layer that runs tesseract.js on each page and draws invisible text at the recognised word boxes. Show a progress bar because OCR is slow.

Storage: persist documents (name, created date, page blobs, per-page settings) in IndexedDB via idb-keyval. Home screen lists saved documents with rename and delete. Nothing syncs.

Also do: a manifest.json and service worker so it installs to the home screen and works offline after first load. Vendor opencv.js and the tesseract worker and eng traineddata locally so offline is real.

Explicitly out of scope: auto-capture, cloud sync, sharing links, signatures, watermarks, any analytics.

No secrets are needed, so no .env. Ship a README with one command to run over HTTPS on a local network so a phone can actually reach it, and a note that camera access requires a secure origin.
